Treatment with biological and targeted synthetic drugs (BMSL) represents a major component of medical intervention for patients in the registry. Between October 1, 2022, and September 30, 2023, a substantial cohort of 360 children and youth, alongside 10,163 adults, received BMSL therapies [^src1]. This highlights the widespread reliance on advanced pharmacological treatments across different age demographics.

Among the specific therapies administered, [[bohj18a1-behandling-med-infliximab|Behandling med infliximab]] (infliximab) is the overwhelmingly dominant choice. It was the most frequently utilized BMSL treatment for children and youth, reaching 239 unique patients (66%), and for adults, with 3,754 unique patients (37%) [^src1]. Further emphasizing its central role, infliximab accounted for 65% of all BMSL treatments in children and 43% in adults [^src2].

Other biological and targeted treatments are used with varying frequency. [[bohj18a3-behandling-med-adalimumab|Behandling med adalimumab]] (adalimumab) was administered to 59 children and youth (16%) and 2,689 adults (26%) during the period [^src1]. [[bohj19h4-behandling-med-vedolizumab|Behandling med vedolizumab]] (vedolizumab) saw usage among 42 children and youth (12%) and 1,735 adults (17%) [^src1]. [[bohj18b3-behandling-med-ustekinumab|Behandling med ustekinumab]] (ustekinumab) was given to 17 children and youth (5%) and 1,604 adults (16%) [^src1]. Finally, [[bohj28d-behandling-med-tofacitinib|Behandling med tofacitinib]] (tofacitinib) was the least common, utilized by only 3 children and youth (1%) and 126 adults (1%) [^src1]. These figures collectively map the landscape of [[Biologiske og målrettede syntetiske lægemidler]] in clinical practice.
